title: Group lines into blocks with indentation
objective: Use indentation to say which lines belong together.

body.text: Lagom does not use braces, and it has no end word to close a block. Instead, a line such as if, repeat or function is followed by lines indented four spaces further in. Those indented lines belong to it. When the indentation goes back to the start of the line, the block is over.

body.title: One block
body.code:
make ready equal to true
if ready is equal to true
    say "start"

body.text: Blocks can be nested. Each extra level of indentation puts a line one level deeper inside the block above it.

body.title: Nested blocks
body.code:
make score equal to 72
if score is greater than 50
    if score is at most 100
        say "valid score"
    say "checked"

body.text: Keep every line of a block at the same depth. A line at a smaller depth ends the block, and the line after it runs once the block is finished.

body.prompt: The loop below counts to 3. Add a line after the loop, not inside it, that says done. The output should be 1, 2, 3 and then done.
body.starter:
make changing count equal to 0
repeat while count is less than 3
    increase count by 1
    say count
body.solution:
make changing count equal to 0
repeat while count is less than 3
    increase count by 1
    say count
say "done"

checks.description: A say "done" line starts at the left edge, after the loop
